Definition: to open up, i.e. (figuratively) interpret (a dream)
BiblicalUsage: Pathar means to open up, to interpret, especially a dream. Joseph says to the butler and the baker in Genesis 40:8, do not interpretations belong to God? Tell me them, I pray you. The butler's dream is interpreted in Genesis 40:16, and Pharaoh's dreams are interpreted in Genesis 41:12 and 41:15, where Joseph says he has heard that he can understand a dream to interpret it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe interpretation belongs to God, and Joseph knew it: the dreams were not his to open, they were God's to explain through him. That is why I hold that the gift of understanding is never a possession, it is a trust, and Joseph used it to save the very people who had sold him.
